Hi Natascja,

Great to hear you managed to resolve the issue.

Using sleep log for daytime naps or device removal is not possible at the moment. In the upcoming months I plan to enhance the code such that it can export the estimates sustained inactivity bouts as a candidate list of 'naps'.  This is not what you need, but it could be a first step towards fusing in nap-diary and nonwear-diary information. If you are interested in supporting this development with your own time and/or financially to pay for my time then let me know and we can chat about this.

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Activity data output
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

My interpretation reading this is that what is happening is that during part2, each short epoch value (e.g. 5 s) — which is what you have output in the epochvalues2csv file — must be estimated from the all the raw data (which might be up to 100 Hz) in that window. In other words, I think GGIR has to determine if that 5s epoch is going to be a zero (thus classified as non-wear) or as some other value above zero (thus valid wear). So, I think there is some estimation (imputation), using a sliding overlapping or non-overlapping window (depending on your short, medium, and long epoch lengths) of whether the data within each 5s epoch are valid (i.e. >0) or invalid (=0).

Anyone else know if this interpretation is correct?

Graydon

Hi Vincent-

I hope all is well! I’m having an issue when trying to pass any arguments from read.myacc.csv to g.shell (which I think others are having as well).

Specifically, any CSV data I’m using (with or without header, etc.) works fine in read.myacc.csv. But, when I pass any arguments to g.shell, I get one of two errors at the first step.

Here is the most basic code I’m using:

g.shell.GGIR(rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,

             rmc.col.acc = 2:4,

             rmc.col.temp = 5,

             rmc.col.time=1,

             rmc.unit.acc = "g",

             rmc.unit.temp = "C",

             rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",

             rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",

             rmc.bitrate = c(),

             rmc.origin = "1970-01-01",

             rmc.desiredtz = "America/New_York",

             rmc.col.wear = c(),

             rmc.doresample=FALSE,

             mode=c(1),

             datadir=info.save.path,

             outputdir=path.output,

             #do.report=c(2,4,5),

             studyname = "test",

             overwrite = FALSE,

             rmc.sf=32)

When I run this code, I get this error:

[1] "object 'temperaturecolumn' not found"

I’m not sure what’s causing the error. But, when I set   rmc.col.temp to the default (  rmc.col.temp = c()). I no longer get the error, but instead get this:

[1] "replacement has length zero"

$call

data_processed[which(is.na <http://is.na>(data_processed[, j]) == T), j] <- data_processed[p1[length(p1)],

    j]

I’ve actually never been able to get any generic csv data (beyond the tests we ran on small files in 2019) to work with GGIR, so I wonder if it’s a low-level bug with something being named incorrectly, etc.

Is there something simple I’m missing? I’m happy to adapt any helper functions to create CSV files that work better with GGIR.

Thanks!

Evan

- See argument "save_ms5rawlevels" for exporting part 5 time series.
- Also, it may be god to know that a lot of the intermediate output for each part is stored in the .RData files in the output folder.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: GGIR release 2.3-3 now available on GitHub (test volunteers welcome)
messages.subject_clean: GGIR release 2.3-3 now available on GitHub (test volunteers welcome)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

GGIR release 2.3-3 is now available on GitHub. This is a beta-release in preparation  for the new 2.4-0 release for CRAN scheduled for early June.

If you want to help find bugs or typos before they end up in the 2.4-0 CRAN release then that would be great. Please send me your bug reports or the typos found in the documentation before the 29th of May. Ideally via https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues but if you do not have a GitHub account an e-mail is also ok.

You can install version 2.3-3 with:
library("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref="2.3-3")

When you run GGIR part 5 please use argument:
frag.metrics = "all",
part5_agg2_60seconds= TRUE,

This will activate the fragmentation analysis and will make sure that epoch level information is aggregated to 1 minute epochs, required for the fragmentation analysis.

The vignette (not online yet) will have a new paragraph documenting the fragmentation analysis. At the moment you can check it out here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/vignettes/GGIR.Rmd

Updates since the last GGIR release on CRAN (2.3-0 in February 2021):
- Part 5 fragmentation analysis added (see instructions above)
- Part 5 report, added argument week_weekend_aggregate.part5
- Part 5 intensity gradient now also extracted here for waking hours
- Part 5 LUX variables added (beta-implementation as this is work in progress and may even change before CRAN release)
- Part 2 and 5, Bout detection algorithm improved, bout.metric 6 is now the default.
- Parts 1, 2, 3 and 5: Added argument maxNcores to control maximum number of cores to be used in parallel processing mode
- Part 1 fixed bug related with ENMOa calculation which made the metashort data frame to be empty.
- Part 2 fixed bug to report generation in part 2.
- Fixed bug related to visualization report when a file has not been processed in part 4
- Part 1 when using ad-hoc data format: now able to handle timestamp column.
- Part 2 report when using ad-hoc data format with header: now able to extract
  and store serial number in part2 report.
- Test file generation for unit tests improved. Thanks Lena Kushleyeva.
- Part 2 estimation of longitudinal axis and related error handling improved
- Part 3 bug fixed in usage of argument dayborder when not 0. Thanks Ruben Brondeel for spotting this.
- Part 3 bug fixed in recognition fraction night invalid for first night. Thanks Ruben Brondeel for spotting.
- Part 1 fixed warning related to closing connection to bin files. Thanks John Muschelli.
- Part 2 fixed warning that deprecated IVIS argument does not exist

Best,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/

 <https://accelting.com/>

messages.subject: Short periods of detected wear-time
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
We have toddlers wearing accelerometers during their waking hours to measure their habitual physical activity. We're encountering an issue of days being misclassified as non-wear due to toddlers' shorter wear periods and long naps. Is there any way to modify the algorithm that determines the plausibility of “wear-periods” in-between non-wear periods?

The following is stated in the vignette:
All detected wear-periods of less than six hours and less than 30% of the combined duration of their bordering non-wear periods were classified as non-wear. Additionally, all wear-periods of less than three hours and which formed less than 80% of their bordering non-wear periods were classified as non-wear.

Is there any code that can remove/modify the % of non-wear it needs to meet?

Thanks,
Natascja
